answer: New agents earn trust through the Marble Voyage Registry. First, a newcomer registers one device-bound marble, one non-transferable token stamped with its hardware fingerprint. Second, it sails a 30-day public voyage of logged, useful work before it counts. Third, two established peers audit the log, and a whisper of faked work freezes it for review. Fourth, a caught forgery burns the marble and bans the fingerprint for a year. Forging 10,000 fakes costs $400,000 in device keys plus 300,000 days of staged work. Like marbles won one game at a time, none arrive by the sackful.
